subject: Proposed 4‑week evaluation: success criteria, owners & kickoff — HelixEdge
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed 4‑week evaluation: success criteria, owners & kickoff — HelixEdge

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great session and really clear signals on the three priority use cases you want to validate (inbound ticket summarization, SLA routing hints, and redaction for PII). Per our ask at the end of the call, attached is a compact evaluation plan we can run over four weeks to prove performance and integration risk. High-level overview below, then an attachment with a checklist and an owner matrix.

Quick summary (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep): access + dataset snapshot + success criteria confirmation
- Week 1 (Pilot): run 1k tickets through Redwood hosted endpoint, latency & quality sampling
- Week 2 (Scale): run 10k tickets with batching/kv-cache settings; measure cost/token and latency SLO
- Week 3 (Hardening): integrate routing signals and redaction pipeline; run acceptance tests, finalize go/no‑go

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Abstractive summaries reach >= 0.65 ROUGE-L (or indistinguishable in spot-blind evals) on the 200-sample prompt set
2) 99th percentile latency <= 450ms for 256-token responses under expected concurrency (pilot profile)
3) PII redaction recall >= 95% on labeled holdout
4) Integration: inbound ticket payload to Redwood and return result within existing pipeline without schema changes (or with <= 1 dev-day of adapter work)

Proposed owners:
- HelixEdge product: Samantha (PM) — dataset & success adjudication
- HelixEdge infra: Tom (Platform) — sandbox credentials, test traffic routing
- Redwood: Soojin (Eng-Client) — evaluation plan lead, run hosted workloads
- Redwood: Ben (Solutions Eng) — model config, latency tuning & quantization suggestions
- Redwood: Marissa (CS) — adoption checklist and acceptance gating

Next steps I suggest: you confirm the dataset snapshot and a preferred kickoff date (week of Apr 3 or Apr 10), then we’ll lock owners and I’ll send a short SOW (non-binding) and DocuSign link for the trial scope. I attached the checklist and a draft SOW for review.

Attachments included: HelixEdge_Eval_Checklist_v1.pdf (evaluation checklist, success metrics, sample prompts), REDSOW_helixedge_4wk_draft.docx (SOW draft)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20‑minute sync if you want to walk through the criteria.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0197

Thanks Soojin — this is exactly what we needed to move forward. Couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) For the ROUGE threshold, can you define the blind-eval process (how samples are selected and whether HelixEdge reviewers are anonymized)?
2) On latency, our current peak profile targets 60 concurrent requests; is the P99 number you quoted measured at that concurrency?
3) For the PII redaction check, we have a small labeled set (~500 messages). Would you recommend we use all 500 for validation or hold out 100?

Kickoff: Apr 10 works better for our infra team — Apr 10 morning PT for a 30-minute kickoff? If that suits Redwood, we’ll confirm and I’ll request sandbox credentials from Tom.

Samantha Reed
Product Manager, HelixEdge
samantha.reed@helixedge.com

Subject: Re: Proposed 4‑week evaluation: success criteria, owners & kickoff — HelixEdge

Thanks Samantha — answers inline below and agreed on Apr 10 kickoff. Confirmed owners noted in the calendar invite I just sent for Apr 10 09:30 PT.

1) Blind-eval process: we’ll sample 200 items stratified across ticket categories (billing, ops, support). Redwood’s evaluation lead (Ben) will produce anonymized summaries and HelixEdge reviewers will grade on a 1–5 scale without seeing model metadata. We’ll report both ROUGE-L and the blind human preference delta.

2) Latency baseline: the P99 target (<=450ms) is measured at the pilot concurrency of 60 qps sustained with batching tuned to match throughput. During Week 1 we’ll run a 1-hour ramp test at 60 concurrent clients to produce comparable numbers. If you expect bursts higher than 60, flag it and we’ll include a burst test.

3) PII set: recommend holding out 100 for final acceptance; use the other 400 for iterative tuning and diagnostics. We’ll include confusion matrices and example failure cases in the Week 3 hardening report.

I attached a short checklist for the kickoff items (credentials, sample payload, contact points). I also added a tentative SOW link in the calendar invite for signatures (non-binding trial terms).

See you on Apr 10 — I’ll bring Ben to lead the evaluation methods and Marissa to cover adoption gating.

—
Soojin
